body.p: Inak. Dea started living with Bunelya and Nibiyu. One day Dea went down the river. One can only hear along the river the sound of the song: Hey, hey, hey. How long he went, and the river became a large lake. Dyooa looks. There is a lean-to at the mouth of the river. A man sits on the lean-to and whittles. His boat is tied to the lean-to leg. Dyooa headed the lean-to. And the man's boat is made of copper, and when he whittles, his shavings turn into birds. This is Inak, thinks Dea. There is a very strong current near the leg of Inak's lean-to, Dyooa's boat almost capsized. Dyooa tied his little boat next to Inak's copper boat. Oh, a guest has come, said Inak. He lowered a ladder from above e. Dea climbed up the ladder. Now they are talking. When they finished their conversations, Inak said. Dyooa, you're hungry, right? Yes, I'm hungry. Inak pulled an iron cable. Serve a man some food! Various kinds of food went up along the iron cable. Dyooa eats very well. Having finished eating, Dyooa said to Inak. When seven days pass, come visit me. Then he went home. One can only hear along the river the sound of the song: Hey, hey, hey. Having reached home, he began to make a lean-to. He made a lean-to and tied his boat to the leg of the lean-to. He put Nibiyu and Bunelya into a bag, gave them various sorts of food and said. When I pull the rope, send me food, my guest will come. He threw his fellows into the water, having tied a stone to the bag. He tied his boat to the leg of the lean-to, he sat down on the lean-to, he looks down, waiting for his guest. As seven days have passed, the boat is moving from below. When he waves his oar, its tracks become like snow. His boat goes very fast. He stopped it near Dyooa's boat. Dyooa's lean-to almost fell into the water. Inak said, Dyooa's lean-to is shaking. No, no, Dea said. Dea lowered from above a ladder for Inak. While Inak was climbing up, Dyooa's lean-to almost fell into the water. Dyooa's lean-to is shaking, Inak said again. No, no, that's how it's supposed to be, said Dyooa. Dyooa whittles, but his shavings only fall into the water and do not become any birds. How much they talk, but finally Dyooa said. Inak, you are hungry, right? If you have something, why wouldn't I be hungry, I've got here from afar. Dyooa pulled his rope. Nothing appears at all. He keeps pulling it, but there is nothing. Your people must have fallen asleep, said Inak, I'll get home somehow. Then he went home.As soon as Inak disappeared behind a cape, Dyooa pulled his people onto his boat. Nibiyu and Bunelya had already died. That's how Inak dealt with me, said Dyooa. He buried his dead people. This is the end.
